title: Vela Systems - Reserved GPU & isolation evaluation
summary: Initial discovery to understand Vela's inference needs: steady baseline traffic for batch scoring, bursty spikes from interactive features, and strict isolation requirements for regulated customers. Discussed host vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs, reserved GPU sizing, prewarm/hotpool strategies, KMS requirements, and next steps for pricing and pilot benchmarks.
next_steps: Jordan to send tiered pricing + commitment options (by 2026-03-05)
Maya to share warm-pool benchmark deck and runbook (by 2026-03-04)
Vela to provide traffic profile CSV and sample prompt set (by 2026-03-06)
Schedule pilot kickoff w/ infra team (target week of 2026-03-09)
action_items: Jordan Price: Prepare committed-use pricing spreadsheet and include dedicated + hybrid hosting scenarios (due 2026-03-05)
Maya Chen: Share warm-pool prewarm benchmarks, KV cache behavior notes, and a proposed pilot test matrix (due 2026-03-04)
Carlos Mendez: Export 2 weeks of traffic by route and sample payloads for benchmarking (due 2026-03-06)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-28 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Price (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood Solutions Eng), Carlos Mendez (CTO, Vela), Priya Rao (Lead ML), Ellen Park (Infra), Samir Gupta (Product)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, appreciate it. we sent the agenda earlier, hope it looks OK, uh we'll go through current stack, traffic, then sizing and isolation.
[00:34] Carlos: Yeah thanks Jordan, quick note, we are evaluating three paths: hosted for quick experiments, Dedicated reserved GPUs for predictable latency and isolation, and Private VPC for a handful of regulated customers. Main ask is consistent tail latency under 200ms for interactive routes.
[01:10] Priya: And we have nightly batch scoring jobs that can be flexed, but interactive chat features spike, like, 6x during product demos. So burst matters.
[01:42] Maya: Nice. quick clarifying question — when you say 6x spike, is that sustained for more than a minute or short blips?
[02:05] Priya: Usually 2-5 minutes, sometimes up to 15 if we push releases. We've seen up to 10k rps across multiple microservices at peak.
[02:38] Liam: And is there a difference between customers? you mentioned regulated tenants — do they need physical isolation or is logical isolation with encryption/KMS enough?
[03:02] Carlos: For Healthcare customers we need audited KMS, SOC2-level logs, and ideally tenant isolation. Preference is dedicated pools per tenant but open to fenced multi-tenant if we can prove blast radius containment.
[03:28] Jordan: That's consistent with other folks. Redwood Dedicated can do dedicated GPU pools and we offer VPC private deployment for on-prem or air-gapped if needed. question on budget brackets — any guardrails?
[03:54] Samir: We're trying to keep committed spend under $X/month for the first phase — not public budget — but that constraints sizing. we want a plan that grows.
[04:20] Maya: Ok, on sizing: Based on what you said, we'd recommend reserving a baseline pool sized for steady-state interactive traffic plus a hotpool for prewarmed nodes to cover bursts. two approaches: 1) larger reserved pool sized for 95th percentile, 2) smaller base + warm pool for spikes. The unit economics differ.
[04:52] Priya: Can you talk about warm pool? how quickly do nodes come online, and what about model load times with big models?
[05:16] Maya: Good Q. cold boot of a new GPU node can be several minutes if you need model weights pulled/compiled. warm-pools maintain model artifacts and warmed KV caches so prewarm latency is low — typically sub 200-300ms for new requests, assuming we pin model variants. for really large models (>50B) we recommend quantized variants on the warm pool.
[05:46] Ellen: Do you support customer-managed KMS/HSM? We can't have keys leave our control.
[06:03] Jordan: Yes — Private deployments integrate with customer KMS; hosted can integrate as well but for full key ownership we recommend Private. We'll attach the KMS integration guide.
[06:26] Carlos: How do you handle evictions and tenant fencing? if one tenant has noisy traffic, we need guarantees it won't affect others.
[06:46] Liam: We use a combination of tenant-level quotas, soft preemption, and strict tenant fencing at the pool level. For regulated tenants we recommend dedicated pools which provide the strongest isolation. There's also per-route rate shaping and circuit-breaker policies.
[07:12] Priya: Any SLA numbers for tail latency on Dedicated?
[07:25] Maya: Our standard SLA for Dedicated is availability and latency targets measured at the model route: e.g., p95 generation latency < 250ms for small-medium models under provisioned conditions; we'll share a performance profile. Note these depend on sequence length and model choice.
[07:52] Jordan: quick interjection — competitors we see referenced are Replicate and CloudA — differences are around operational tooling and warm-pool behavior.
[08:12] Carlos: We had a Replicate PoC, warm pools were inconsistent, that was a blocker.
[08:28] Samir: Also cost — we need to show unit economics vs running internal infra.
[08:44] Maya: We can run a benchmark with your traffic to compare per-token cost and tail latency. For pilots we usually run a 2-week dedicated baseline with synthetic bursts derived from your profile.
[09:05] Priya: On model versions — we need pinning and quick rollbacks for safety. how do rollouts work?
[09:22] Liam: Redwood supports version pinning, canary traffic splits, and automatic fallback to smaller/cheaper model variants if errors or resource constraints hit.
[09:42] Ellen: For external auditors, we need access logs and an audit trail.
[09:55] Jordan: We expose audit logs, tokenized usage, and per-request traces in Redwood Console — can export for your SI. we'll include a logging sample.
[10:18] Carlos: Let's talk numbers — based on 10k peak RPS and 6x spikes, what are rough GPU counts?
[10:35] Maya: rough back-of-envelope: depends on model. if you're using a 13B/model optimized on A100 or equivalent we might need N GPUs for baseline; for spikes we size hotpool for concurrent requests. We should run an initial capacity model using your payload sizes.
[11:02] Priya: Our average prompt is 320 tokens, sometimes up to 1k for long-form. Batch scoring runs overnight and can be on cheaper nodes.
[11:27] Liam: Good to know. that increases memory and kv cache pressure. prewarming KV helps a lot for long contexts.
[12:00] Samir: Curious about autoscaling — can Dedicated scale out automatically or is that manual?
[12:17] Maya: Dedicated supports autoscaling within configured policies and burst into pre-defined surge capacity if available. For hard isolation customers we often recommend reserved capacity with configured burst windows.
[12:36] Carlos: What about preemption risk and node churn? We operate in a heavily regulated environment; preemption could break SLAs.
[12:51] Liam: For Dedicated we avoid preemptible hardware for regulated pools; burst can be handled with non-preemptible warm-pool nodes or by routing to a different region/fallback model.
[13:14] Priya: How do you measure cost impact of warm pool? I want a number we can show to finance.
[13:28] Jordan: We typically produce a per-hour reserved cost plus the marginal cost of warm instances. We'll include sample math in the pricing spreadsheet.
[13:40] Maya: Example: small warm n1 nodes cost X/hr and cover ~Y QPS for a given model — we'll include with the benchmark results.
[14:02] Carlos: Security question — SSO and RBAC, we use SAML and need fine-grained roles for engineers vs auditors.
[14:15] Jordan: Redwood supports SAML SSO and RBAC. We can map groups to least-privilege roles. For Private deployments you can sync with your IdP.
[14:36] Ellen: Any compliance certifications? SOC2?
[14:44] Jordan: Yes, Redwood is SOC2 Type II; for Private deployments we provide the control evidence and audit artifacts. We'll attach compliance pack.
[15:05] Priya: When you talk about fallback models, do you mean smaller models or local on-prem replicas?
[15:19] Maya: Both. fallback is policy driven — you can fallback to a smaller quantized model variant or route to an approximation model to preserve response time. for high-security customers, private on-prem replica is an option.
[15:44] Samir: What about model loading time when switching variants during a spike?
[15:56] Maya: That's why warm pools typically maintain the top variants; when switching we prefer to route rather than load in-line. load in-line can be expensive for large weights.
[16:18] Carlos: Ok. let's talk pilot scope. We'd like to validate tail latency and cost over 2 weeks on dedicated. what's your recommended pilot?
[16:32] Maya: Two-week pilot on a mid-sized dedicated pool with warm-pool for peak windows, run your production traffic replayed plus synthetic bursts. We'll instrument p50/p95/p99 and per-route cost.
[16:50] Priya: We can replay a week's traffic easily. we'll anonymize.
[17:03] Jordan: Good. we'll need sample prompt set, payload sizes, and expected concurrency per route.
[17:18] Carlos: One final engineering question — do you support private network peering (VPC peering) and ingress controls?
[17:30] Liam: Yes, VPC peering and private link options are supported for Private. Hosted can limit egress and support customer IP allow lists, but peering is for Private deployments.
[17:50] Ellen: Ops-wise, who will run the pilot config — do we need our infra folks or do you manage?
[17:58] Jordan: We do the heavy lifting for pilot setup; we ask for a point of contact on your side for approvals and access. After pilot we hand over runbooks.
[18:12] Samir: Timeframe — how quickly can pilot start?
[18:19] Maya: Once we have traffic and credentials, typical lead time is 2 weeks to standing pilot. depends on region and model onboarding.
[18:33] Carlos: Ok, sounds reasonable. are there any gotchas we should know?
[18:41] Maya: Watch out for long tail token lengths — they blow up mem and latency. also, third-party LLM libs sometimes cause longer cold-starts.
[18:55] Priya: question about data retention — we need strict PII rules. can you redact or avoid retaining prompts?
[19:08] Jordan: Yes, retention policies configurable; we can disable storage for certain routes and provide masked logs. for Private you control data retention fully.
[19:24] Priya: good.
[19:28] (crosstalk)
[19:40] Maya: I'll draft suggested baseline config: pool sizes, warmpool counts, prewarm window schedule, and a sample rollback policy.
[19:52] Jordan: We'll attach pricing examples and the SOC2/compliance packet.
[20:05] Carlos: Great. A few off-the-cuff numbers: we're comfortable starting with a baseline equivalent to 8 A100s and a warm pool of 4 to cover spikes, but this is fuzzy.
[20:25] Liam: We'll validate with your traffic, might shift depending on model and quantization.
[20:38] Priya: For the pilot, will you provide monitoring dashboards?
[20:45] Maya: Yes — Redwood Console will show per-route latency, token counts, cache hits, and cost breakdowns. We'll add tracing hooks.
[21:01] Ellen: Can you export SIEM-friendly logs?
[21:07] Jordan: Yes, we'll provide log forwarding and structured JSON logs.
[21:20] Samir: Budget question again — if we commit to a quarterly reserved capacity, do you offer discounts?
[21:33] Jordan: Yep — committed plans get step discounts; we'll include tiered discounts in the pricing doc.
[21:44] Carlos: Any special networking things for hybrid on-prem nodes?
[21:52] Liam: We'll need a VPN and secure peering; for air-gapped we have an on-prem package. we'll detail in the deployment options doc.
[22:08] Priya: For the bench tests, can we include our custom tokenizer and prompt templates?
[22:16] Maya: We can — provide them and we'll run them in the pilot harness.
[22:28] (short pause)
[22:35] Carlos: Alright, let's list the immediate deliverables.
[22:40] Jordan: Jordan -> pricing + commitment options; Maya -> warm-pool benchmarks, runbook, pilot matrix; Vela -> traffic csv and prompt set. Also set a tentative kickoff for week of March 9th.
[23:02] Priya: Sounds good. One more: cost center tagging on usage for chargebacks.
[23:12] Jordan: Supported — we'll add tags to the billing export.
[23:22] Samir: Any final concerns?
[23:28] Ellen: Make sure the audit artifacts include KMS rotation history.
[23:35] Jordan: Noted. we'll include KMS rotation evidence in the compliance pack.
[23:45] (wrap-up)
[24:00] Jordan: Thanks folks, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule.

Recap/Notes:
- Pilot: 2-week dedicated pilot with warm-pool; Redwood to run with Vela traffic replay + synthetic bursts.
- Focus metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, per-route token cost, cache hit rates, cold-start frequency.
- Compliance: SOC2 pack + KMS integration guide + logs export.
- Next meeting: Pilot kickoff week of 2026-03-09

End of transcript.
